subject: Helium Bank - Hosted API: data retention & deletion details
messages:
From: Elisabeth Turner <elisabeth.turner@heliumbank.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliumbank.com
Date: 2027-05-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Hosted API retention & deletion specifics

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this through our security questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our side to finalize the Helium Bank assessment:

- Can you confirm the exact retention windows for (a) request/response logs, (b) KV/prefix caches, and (c) long-term telemetry/metrics tied to tenant IDs for your hosted API?
- When a customer requests erasure for a tenant, what is the end-to-end timeline for deletion from primary stores, cache layers, and backups? Do you provide any proof or attestation?
- Are backups immutable snapshots or can they be modified/expunged on request? If snapshots persist, what is the process to ensure customer data is purged from them?

We’re aiming to get this answered by EOD Thursday to keep procurement on schedule.

Appreciate it — Elisabeth
Information Security | Helium Bank
[Helium Bank HQ]

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elisabeth Turner <elisabeth.turner@heliumbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API retention & deletion specifics

Elisabeth —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching a short summary PDF and a diagram of our data flows for the hosted API. Markus (security) and Jordan (CS/ops) are looped in for the technical and operational details.

1) Retention windows (default / can be configured per-tenant):
   - Request/response logs: default 30 days; configurable 7–90 days on hosted plans.
   - KV/prefix caches (temporary inference caches): ephemeral by default (TTL 24 hours); persistent cache snapshots only used for performance debugging and retained for up to 7 days unless customer requests otherwise.
   - Telemetry/metrics (tenant-aggregated): 13 months by default; retained without request/response payloads (no raw user content).

2) Erasure timeline (customer-initiated tenant erase request):
   - T0: Request received by support or API -> we validate scope (24 hours).
   - T+24–72 hours: Delete primary records and clear active cache entries.
   - T+72–168 hours (3–7 days): Purge from secondary/replicated stores; we run a tenant-scope KV sweep and verify tombstones.
   - Backups/snapshots: see 3) below.

3) Backups & snapshots:
   - Backups are daily point-in-time snapshots stored for 14–30 days depending on plan. Snapshots are immutable in our store to preserve recovery guarantees. For erasure requests we perform a snapshot-mediated scrub: we restore the minimal snapshot to an isolated environment, remove the tenant data, re-seal and replace the snapshot chain. This process is executed by our on-call infra team and typically completes within 7–30 days depending on retention window and schedule.
   - We provide a signed attestation (pdf) on request once scrub/replace is complete.

4) Evidence and proof:
   - We can provide an operational runbook describing the scrub process, an audit log extract for the tenant, and a signed attestation PDF.

Next steps: Markus will add technical specifics about snapshot storage and encryption; Jordan will add the operator checklist for scrub jobs. I’ve attached: retention-policy-summary.pdf and data-handling-diagram.png.

Best,
Grace Occonnor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace — that helps. A couple clarifying questions before we sign off:

- For the snapshot-mediated scrub (replace workflow), can you clarify whether the old immutable snapshot is retained (in an archive) after the scrub/replace? If so, for how long and can we require deletion as part of the contract?
- Does the attestation include a hash or certificate tied to the replaced snapshot so we can independently verify the scrub?
- For enterprise orgs, do you offer shorter default retention windows (e.g., 30 days for telemetry) and faster scrub SLAs for backups?

Procurement would like a DocuSign addendum to capture the scrub SLA and attestation delivery timeline if possible.

Cheers,
Elisabeth

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elisabeth Turner <elisabeth.turner@heliumbank.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API retention & deletion specifics

Elisabeth —

Technical follow-up from security/ops on the snapshot question and contractual options:

- Immutable snapshot archive policy: snapshots are immutable at rest for auditability. We retain snapshot artifacts for the configured retention period (14–30 days) in encrypted object storage. After a scrub/replace operation we mark the original snapshot as superseded and remove accessible indices; the raw archive object is rotated and re-encrypted. We retain the original binary for an additional 7 days for forensic rollback, after which it is securely shredded (zeroed, metadata scrubbed) by our storage provider. The entire lifecycle is logged to our audit system.

- Contractual deletion: we can include an addendum that requires us to shorten the post-scrub archive hold (for enterprise plans) to 0–7 days with a corresponding fee for shortened retention. That addendum will also state the attestation delivery timeline.

- Attestation & verification: our attestation includes a statement of operations, the scrub job run-id, timestamp, and a SHA-256 digest of the re-sealed snapshot artifact (we provide the digest/hash). You can use the digest to verify the artifact we return (we can make the re-sealed artifact available for your validation in a temporary read-only bucket).

- SLAs for enterprise: yes — we offer configurable retention defaults and expedited scrub workflows (3–7 day target) on enterprise/Dedicated plans. For hosted API customers we support addendums for accelerated timelines.

Attachments: backup-deletion-playbook.txt (operator checklist) and a draft DocuSign addendum (docusign-erasure-addendum.docx).

Let us know preferred timeline for the addendum and whether Helium Bank requires the re-sealed artifact to be uploaded to your validation bucket. Happy to schedule a short call to walk through the scrub playbook.

—Markus Klein
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
